newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday February 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday February 26.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi easily won a confidence vote in the lower house of parliament on Tuesday, called to sweep aside opposition amendments to the final section of the 1997 austerity budget. The vote was carried out by 308 to 257 with one abstention (all).

* Hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti promised to support the confidence motion but he repeated his concerns about another round of belt-tightening. Bertinotti told reporters his party considered the mini-budget to be unnecessary but was open to talks, yet it could not accept any further cut in social spending or additional taxes (all).

* The new board of Italian state controlled telecommunication holding STET, nominated on Tuesday for a three-year mandate, could see changes following the group's privatisation, chairman Guido Rossi said. Addressing his first shareholders' meeting he added that when the privatisation process is achieved he will step down. This afternoon the board is expected to hold another meeting (all).

* Italian car maker Fiat said it was not interested in taking a stake in Turin-based banking group Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino. In a statement, Fiat said it ruled out any interest in entering the capital of the banking group. Italy's largest commercial bank had previously announced it was offering 45 percent of its capital currently owned by the foundation San Paolo Holding in a public share offer and a private placement with institutional investors.

* The sale of Olivetti's PC division to a consortium of investors led by U.S. businessman Edward Gottesmann, which should have been completed by February 28, is said to be delayed by a few weeks (Corriere della Sera).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
